beats.say: On Friday, the FAA held departures at every airport in the US.
The reason: communication problems at several of its big air traffic control centers.
Towers only handle takeoffs and landings. In between, huge regional centers guide the planes.
Each center sees planes through faraway radar sites, and talks to pilots through faraway radio sites.
All of that reaches the center over telecom lines. If they fail, controllers can lose the picture, or the voice.
So the safe move is a ground stop. New flights wait at the gate.
Planes already flying keep going and land. Fewer planes means less to watch while systems are down.
The FAA hasn't said exactly what broke. Outages like this usually start with a cut cable or a failed network box.
Flights restart as centers recover. But planes and crews are stuck in the wrong cities, so cancellations spill into the next day.
